ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory customer due diligence under CSSF Regulation 12-02 and the Law of 12 November 2004, requiring extraction of direct and indirect UBOs at the 25% threshold and verification of identity and address. All general partners, managers and UBOs must be screened for politically exposed persons (PEP) status using the PEP categories of Article 1(12) of the Law of 12 November 2004 as amended, supplemented by EU Council guidance. Negative screening is mandatory against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, United Nations Security Council consolidated list, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists (required because the target payment rails, Stripe and Amazon Pay, settle in USD), the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF) indicators, CSSF warnings, and adverse media and corporate disqualification databases. Any PEP or sanctioned-jurisdiction nexus triggers enhanced due diligence, including source of wealth and source of funds documentation, senior management approval, and enhanced ongoing monitoring. CDD files must be retained for at least five years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), electronic submission through the MyLBR portal at www.lbr.lu and the official Ministry of Justice e-filing platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Constitutional instruments and the registered name must be drafted in French, German or Luxembourgish. The registered name must appear in Latin script; Chinese characters, Cyrillic, Arabic or other non-Latin scripts require certified transliteration into Latin characters prior to filing, with the original script recorded only in the KYC/UBO background file. The legal-form complement 'SCSp' or the full phrase 'Société en commandite spéciale' must immediately precede or follow the commercial name. The name must not violate public order or morality and must not mislead the public regarding regulated financial activities or affiliation with the Luxembourg State, municipal authorities or international organizations.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Chambre de Commerce or Chamber of Commerce
PFS or Professional of the Financial Sector (reserved for CSSF-regulated firms)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The RCS freezes the validated name during the filing review and maintains that reservation for 30 calendar days. A single extension of up to 30 additional days may be requested in writing by the licensed filing agent before expiry. On final rejection: (1) the filing agent files an administrative reconsideration (recours gracieux) with the RCS legal division within 15 working days, appending a trademark search report and a clarified statement of distinctiveness; (2) if the RCS maintains the refusal, a judicial appeal may be lodged with the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg, chambre commerciale) within three months of notification of the refusal; (3) in parallel, any third-party opposition under trademark law should be monitored through the Registre des Marques of the LBR. Estimated appeal cost: USD 2,000 to 3,500 for counsel fees plus court costs.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for this non-regulated SCSp: the SCSp must maintain a physical registered office in Luxembourg and, absent operational premises, must appoint a licensed commercial domiciliation agent regulated under the Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of companies. A pure virtual mailbox without a recognized Luxembourg street address is not accepted by the RCS. Because the activity profile is import, laser assembly and resale of wooden puzzles with no regulated financial services, no CSSF licence, no minimum substance ratio, and no specific occupational premises requirement is triggered. However, any hiring of employees, warehousing of inventory, or operation of cutting machinery in Luxembourg will require an identifiable operational address, appropriate work-safety permits, and employee social registration.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Protection Agency), Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class 2 'établissement classé' – simple declaration (notification) under the amended Law of 23 September 2011 on integrated environmental management; wood processing capacity below Annex II thresholds, therefore full EIA report is not required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater to municipal sewer per the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 15 September 2016: COD ≤ 300 mg/L, BOD5 ≤ 30 mg/L, TSS ≤ 60 mg/L, pH 6.0-9.5. Laser-cutting smoke must be extracted through HEPA/activated-carbon filtration meeting the VOC limits of the Law of 21 June 1999 (solvent consumption < 15 t/yr triggers a solvent management plan). Wood dust occupational exposure limit of 2 mg/m³ per ITM. Segregated wood-waste disposal per the amended Law of 21 March 2012.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety certificate (Certificat de sécurité incendie) issued by CGDIS and the communal fire inspector after inspection; structural load inspection certificate approved by an engineer for industrial machinery; ITM workplace clearance confirming CE-marked laser equipment, emergency exits, ventilation, noise levels not exceeding 80 dB(A) and mandatory personal protective equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) for direct taxes, corporate income tax and net wealth tax; Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and registration duties. Central electronic platforms: Guichet.lu / myGuichet (national administrative portal), Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online RCS portal (www.lbr.lu), and the eTVA / eSpace Déclarant (ESD) electronic filing system for VAT returns, listings and declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Incorporate the SCSp by notarial or private deed and file the instrument with the RCS through the LBR/Guichet.lu single window; the SCSp obtains a statutory 15-digit national identification number (matricule / numéro d'identification national), which constitutes the entity TIN and is referenced on the RCS extract; no minimum capital is required. Step 2 - Register for Luxembourg VAT (TVA) with the AEDT before commencing taxable supplies by filing Form 6401 (déclaration d'assujettissement); the AEDT issues the Luxembourg VAT identification number (format LU00000000). Step 3 - Register the SCSp with the ACD through the ESD corporate tax module, file the annual partnership and partner allocation information returns where a Luxembourg-resident general partner or a Luxembourg permanent establishment exists, and obtain confirmation of the fiscally transparent status. Step 4 - For binding certainty on pass-through classification, VAT treatment of export supplies and hybrid mismatch outcomes, file an advance tax ruling request (résolution anticipée) with the ACD before the first taxable transaction; rulings are typically issued within three months. Non-resident ownership is unrestricted, and no separate municipal tax registration exists in this unitary national jurisdiction.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible / Territorial_Scope - The SCSp (Société en Commandite Spéciale) is fiscally transparent by default for Luxembourg direct taxes: corporate income tax and municipal business tax are assessed at the partner level, and net wealth tax is borne by corporate partners; resident partners are taxed on worldwide income, non-resident partners only on Luxembourg-source income effectively connected with a Luxembourg permanent establishment. For VAT, however, the SCSp is a taxable person in its own name: it registers, issues invoices, files returns and claims input VAT credits and refunds; export zero-rating is claimed in the name of the SCSp.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box election, but Article 3(2) LIR allows a partnership (including an SCSp) to elect treatment as an opaque corporate taxpayer subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax; the election is filed with the ACD and binds for a minimum of five years. Under the ATAD 2 hybrid-mismatch framework as implemented in the LIR, a reverse-hybrid SCSp is recharacterized as a Luxembourg resident taxpayer on its undistributed income where another jurisdiction treats the SCSp as opaque and the income would otherwise escape taxation; partner-jurisdiction classification outcomes (for example a US Section 7701 check-the-box election on the SCSp) are assessed for hybrid mismatch purposes, and advance tax rulings can confirm the transparency or opacity outcome before operations commence.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA - Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée), implemented under the Luxembourg VAT Law (LTV) and harmonized with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC; Luxembourg applies no separate GST or sales and use tax within its unitary national territory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 of annual taxable turnover exclusive of VAT (small-business 'franchise en base' exemption under Article 57 LTV; EUR 30,000 until 31 December 2024); mandatory VAT registration with the AEDT arises immediately upon exceeding the threshold. A separate EUR 10,000 annual threshold applies to intra-EU distance sales of goods and digital services under the OSS (One-Stop-Shop) scheme, above which Luxembourg VAT is chargeable and returnable through the OSS portal; no sub-national indirect tax registration exists.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC) platform, digital stamping or invoice authorization regime applies in Luxembourg. A B2B e-invoicing mandate takes effect on 1 January 2026: every Luxembourg-established taxable person must issue structured electronic invoices in the EU standard format (XML / EN 16931) for domestic B2B supplies taxable in Luxembourg, transmit them electronically with interoperability through the PEPPOL network, and retain the machine-readable invoice and transmission trail. Non-compliance attracts administrative fines under the LTV and creates documentary deficiencies in export-refund and audit review procedures.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically dispatched or transported out of the EU customs territory to a third country are taxable at 0% under Article 56 LTV, provided the goods leave the EU within 90 days of dispatch and the exporter holds the transport and customs evidence; related input VAT on production (CO2 laser cutting, wood and plywood inputs, packaging, logistics) is deductible and any excess input VAT credit is reimbursed by the AEDT in the periodic VAT refund cycle. Services supplied to non-EU business customers (design, assembly services, software, royalties and related technical services) fall outside Luxembourg VAT under the place-of-supply rules of Article 17 LTV, with the customer's country applying reverse charge or local assessment; proof of the customer's non-EU establishment and valid VAT identification is required. Export operations are not subject to Luxembourg customs duties on exit, and zero-rating entitlement is substantiated through the export documentation bundle and the inward remittance evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (EX-A export formalities lodged with the Luxembourg Customs and Excise Administration under the EU Customs Code; retained copy of the electronic export declaration and the export summary)
Bill of Lading / CMR / Air Waybill, stamped or signed by the transporter, evidencing physical departure of the goods from the EU customs territory

Inward Remittance Certificate - bank credit advice, SWIFT/MT103 or account statement evidencing final settlement of export proceeds within the repatriation window (customary export-proof requirement of the AEDT and Luxembourg banks, notwithstanding the absence of statutory exchange controls)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and ACD conduct ex-post documentary audits of export supplies; on request, the exporter must produce the complete evidence bundle within the statutory response period, generally one month, extendable on justified grounds. Failure of proof retroactively revokes the 0% rate: 17% Luxembourg VAT is assessed on the export invoice, late-payment interest accrues from the original VAT return due date, and the clawback is executed through rectified VAT returns. Assessment and clawback rights lapse after five years, extended to ten years where fraud is established. Intentional or materially false zero-rating claims, forged transport documentation, or schemes under which the goods never left the EU are prosecuted as tax fraud under the LTV: administrative fines from EUR 250 to EUR 25,000, criminal fines up to double the evaded VAT, and imprisonment of up to five years for aggravated fraud; collateral consequences include refusal or withdrawal of tax clearance certificates, enhanced multi-year audit cycles before both tax administrations, and de-risking action by payment processors such as Stripe and Amazon Pay.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), a constituent member of the Eurosystem and the European System of Central Banks; prudential banking supervision within the Grand Duchy is exercised jointly by the BCL and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), which acts as the AML/CFT supervisory authority and licensing body for banks and payment institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg enjoys full and unrestricted currency convertibility as a euro-area member state. The euro (EUR) is the sole legal tender. There are no exchange-control laws, no requirement for central-bank approval of cross-border capital movements, and no restriction on capital-account transactions, as the free movement of capital, payments, and investment is guaranteed by Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU). Profit distribution and capital repatriation by an SCSp to non-resident partners (including US, Asian, and other non-EU investors) may be effected without prior BCL or CSSF authorisation, provided that the payee's beneficial ownership is fully documented and that no EU/UN/OFAC sanctions list hits are triggered. The only compliance overlay is the European macro-prudential statistical framework: banks automatically report cross-border transactions on behalf of resident clients to the BCL Balance of Payments (BOP/ITRS) reporting system for any payment of EUR 12,500 or above; such reporting is self-executing by the banking counterparty and does not impose a client-specific authorisation burden.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export-proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion rules in Luxembourg. A Luxembourg exporter (including an SCSp selling wooden puzzles through e-commerce rails or wholesale trade channels) is under no obligation to repatriate, convert, or deposit export receipts into a domestic account within any prescribed timeline. Export proceeds denominated in foreign currency (e.g., USD, GBP, CNY) may be retained freely in foreign-currency accounts or converted into EUR at commercial market rates selected by the treasurer. The only applicable duties are documentary: the SCSp must reflect export proceeds in its VAT returns (where the place of supply is B2C within the EU or intra-EU distance sales), maintain transfer-pricing documentation for cross-border related-party trade, and preserve underlying customs/invoice evidence for bank BOP coding verification.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate-to-High, with structural limitations. A Luxembourg-authorised Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licensed by the CSSF under the amended Law of 21 December 2009, or an EEA EMI passporting into Luxembourg under PSD2, can provide the SCSp with EUR IBANs, multi-currency virtual accounts, SWIFT/SEPA payment initiation, and FX conversion at transparent rates, and can settle Stripe/Amazon Payouts efficiently. However, an EMI is not a credit institution: it cannot grant credit, cannot provide documentary letters of credit, cannot hold client funds for more than a limited safeguarded period, and is not an acceptable venue for partner capital escrow where third-party investor protection is expected. UK-authorised and non-EEA EMIs (including US money transmitters) may not onboard a Luxembourg SCSp after the Brexit transition without a Luxembourg branch or an EEA passport, and any account servicing that suggests deposit-taking outside the EMI perimeter triggers CSSF enforcement. Therefore the recommended architecture is: (i) a Tier-1 commercial bank as the
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The onboarding regime is hybrid with a de facto physical-identification bias for SCSp vehicles. Under the amended CSSF Regulation 12-02 and the Luxembourg Law of 25 March 2020 (emergency digital onboarding measures), the general partner or its effective manager (dirigeant effectif) may in principle complete identification through a certified video conference with a qualified notary, or through bank-approved video KYC, provided the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) supplies a certified true copy of a valid passport and a residential address proof dated within 3 months. In practice, BGL BNP Paribas, BIL, Société Générale Luxembourg, and ING Luxembourg require for SCSp structures: (i) a notarised or apostilled deed of the general partner's resolution authorising account opening; (ii) an in-person or video interview of the natural person(s) holding the 'dirigeant effectif' role; (iii) submission of the signed original partnership agreement (A&L) and the deed of appointment of the general partner; and (iv) a certified copy of the RCS (Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register) extract with the UBO declaration registry reference. If the general partner is a Luxembourg corporate vehicle (e.g., a Lux SARL or another SCSp), the bank will assess the substance of that vehicle and typically still require a physical meeting of its directors at the bank's premises in Luxembourg City before the first credit entry is allowed. Remote-only opening without any in-person interview is generally not granted for non-resident partnerships with foreign UBOs; remote opening is more readily authorised for a fully Luxembourg-resident management structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity in the beneficial-ownership cascade beyond the SCSp contractual chain (e.g., UBOs registered in Jersey, the British Virgin Islands, or a FATF grey-list jurisdiction; layered partnerships of more than three tiers).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Full organisational chart linking every partner to a natural-person UBO; (ii) executed partnership agreement (A&L) showing capital commitments and profit-sharing percentages; (iii) RCS UBO declaration filing receipt; (iv) signed sworn declaration from each intermediary partner confirming no undisclosed beneficial owner; (v) if the UBO is a high-risk jurisdiction resident, a certified legal opinion from a Luxembourg notary or avocat confirming non-identification as a politically exposed person and no sanctions linkage; (vi) source-of-wealth statement backed by the UBO's personal tax returns and bank references.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital injection exceeding EUR 100,000 from a non-EU parent without verifiable commercial or investment rationale (potential disguised third-party funds movement).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Notarised capital contribution or share-premium deed referencing the SCSp's account ID; (ii) parent board resolution authorising the injection; (iii) audited or management-accredited financial statements of the parent for the last two fiscal years; (iv) underlying bank transaction trail from the parent's source account (e.g., USD-denominated corporate treasury liquidation statement); (v) business plan with pro-forma cash-flow projections for the wooden-puzzle laser-assembly production cycle; (vi) confirmation of BOP purpose code 8-Direct/Equity Capital on the incoming SWIFT MT103.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-mismatch red flag: procurement of laser-cutting machinery or raw materials from China PRC suppliers routed via third-party payment agents or shell purchasing houses, creating a divergence between commercial invoice value and settlement value.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Finalised purchase contracts (CIF/FOB Incoterms) with each PRC factory; (ii) original commercial invoices, packing lists, and airway/bill-of-lading documents tied to the goods; (iii) supplier KYC file (business licence translation, bank account confirmation from the PRC supplier's bank); (iv) pro-forma invoice plus QR code customs declaration if imported via EU customs procedures; (v) MOFCOM/relevant Chinese export-licence certification if the machinery is subject to export control; (vi) reconciliation ledger mapping each MT103 payment to a unique invoice number and customs reference.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity e-commerce receivables concentration from Amazon Pay and Stripe with rapid onward distribution, raising perceived layering or sale-of-goods provenance concerns (e.g., drop-shipping without proof of physical stock).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Seller central / Stripe payouts reports showing gross sales per period; (ii) warehouse storage agreements and inventory-count certificates; (iii) VAT reporting export evidence (customs export declarations for non-EU B2C, OSS-VAT returns for EU B2C); (iv) chargeback and refund statistics showing normal retail profile; (v) annual audit opinion or review engagement on the SCSp's revenues; (vi) documented supply-chain flow from PRC/other third-country factory to Luxembourg fulfilment centre or EU warehouse; (vii) pro-active engagement with the bank's KYC periodic-review team by delivering the compliance pack every 12 months.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex multi-jurisdictional structure involving 'Luxembourg SCSp + Delaware LLC + Cayman LP' used by non-EU fund promoters, triggering substance and economic-purpose scrutiny.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: (i) Luxembourg tax-residence certificate and substance file (premises lease, payroll slips, director time-tracking or attendance records); (ii) US tax the substance in the Delaware LLC (if known, trace TIN/EIN evidence and state-franchise-tax filing); (iii) Cayman economic-substance (ES) filing certificate confirming the vehicle performs only pure-holding activity; (iv) written explanation of the commercial value of each layer; (v) consolidated group auditor's letter confirming non-avoidance purpose; (vi) CRS self-certification (Form CRC) and FATCA W-8/W-9 suite for each partner; (vii) fund or investment-advisory agreement specifying the SCSp's operational mandate for the wooden-puzzle venture.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity and capital contributions must enter exclusively through a Luxembourg-licensed banking counterpart to ensure BOP statistical capture and AML log integrity. Recommended protocol: (i) the parent or contributing partner instructs a SWIFT MT103 from its home jurisdiction using the SCSp's bank account IBAN (LU + 28-digit format); (ii) the payment carries the exact narrative referencing the SCSp name and contribution deed date, and uses the ECB/BCL BOP purpose code 8 (Direct Investment / Equity Capital) — or, if the contribution is a shareholder loan, purpose code 9 (Loans) — as declared by the ordering customer to its bank; (iii) the bank will automatically report the transaction to the BCL BOP system without requiring client-specific filing when the amount is at or above EUR 12,500; (iv) the SCSp's general partner must, within 30 days of receipt, deposit a notarised contribution confirmation or a board resolution into the corporate file to be made available on request to the CSSF or the bank's periodic review; (v) for funds originating from non-EU jurisdictions with strict capital controls (e.g., China PRC), the sending bank's approval record must be provided to prove the outward remittance was authorised under the relevant country's SAFE/FDI rules; (vi) funds must remain in the Luxembourg account for a minimum economic holding period aligned with the cash-flow plan to avoid any perception of round-tripping; (vii) any conversion of injected foreign currency (USD, CNY) into EUR is executed by the Luxembourg bank at agreed commercial rates, with the FX gain/loss booked in the SCSp's treasury ledger.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements, the SCSp treasury should operate a two-rail clearing architecture. (i) Intra-EEA payments (suppliers in Germany, Portugal, Poland, or Ireland, and EU logistics providers) are settled via SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) using the same-day TARGET2 real-time rail or SEPA Instant; outbound SEPA messages must include the structured creditor reference matching the invoice, and any EUR transaction near or above EUR 12,500 is captured automatically in the BCL BOP report; (ii) non-EEA payments (PRC lenders, US machinery vendors) are cleared through SWIFT MT103 with standard field 50F ordering-party identification and field 72 remittance information; the bank will apply an OFAC/EU-sanctions and adverse-media screen on every beneficiary, and the compliance file should pre-empt any blocked-party hit by supplying the Beneficiary Identification (LEI or registration number); (iii) for large procurement contracts (e.g., purchase of a CO2 laser cutting line exceeding EUR 50,000), a documentary letter of credit (Commercial LC) is issued by the Luxembourg bank via SWIFT MT700, with MT707 amendment messages for any variation; the LC must be payable in EUR or a fully convertible trade currency (USD, CNY only where the China desk confirms CNY-clearing capability); (iv) no outbound disbursement should be executed to a private crypto or digital-asset intermediary; all disbursements must land on a named corporate bank account matching the underlying commercial contract; (v) VAT is handled separately in the customs/procurement flow: non-EU principals are invoiced on a reverse-charge basis, and import VAT is reported in the Luxembourg monthly VAT return; the bank is not involved in VAT clearing unless the SCSp opts for a VAT deferral arrangement requiring customs-bonded account attestation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable EUR/CNY foreign-exchange forward contracts (spot-lag or forward outright, tenors up to 12 months) executed with the Luxembourg Tier-1 bank under ISDA / master agreement; mandatory EMIR reporting and initial margin exchange if the daily average gross notional exceeds EUR 8 billion (rarely applicable, but collateral posting per CSA still required).

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on offshore CNH (and restricted currencies where physical delivery is unavailable) for hedging CNY purchases from PRC suppliers; NDFs are permitted because they settle in EUR and avoid CNY convertibility restrictions; each NDF requires a documented underlying trade forecast and no rolling speculative rebooking.

Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and EUR/CNH) transacted under the ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with Credit Support Annex (CSA) to align borrowing or revenue currency mismatches; permitted solely for cash-flow tenor conversion and not for leveraged treasury speculation.

Vanilla EUR/CNY and EUR/USD FX options (call EUR / put foreign currency) for purchase-side hedging, with premium paid upfront from the SCSp's operational treasury account; short (written) options are not permitted without separate board approval.

Plain-vanilla FX swap points transactions (tom-next rollovers and short-dated swaps) used to manage intra-month settlement liquidity between multi-currency accounts without altering the underlying economic exposure.

Spot forwards for EUR/USD legacy e-commerce proceeds (Amazon Pay and Stripe settlement currencies) where daily payouts are accumulated and converted at prevailing mid-market rates; the treasury policy caps daily conversion execution at one order per day to minimise slippage and preserve auditability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts (dépôt des comptes annuels) with balance sheet, profit and loss statement and annexes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / Luxembourg Business Registers, Luxembourg
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval by the partners and no later than seven months after the financial year-end (31 July for a 31 December year-end); transitional RCS digital-filing extension to the following 31 December may apply
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: RCS injunction after expiry; court-appointed default filing agent at the SCSp's expense; criminal fines of EUR 500 to EUR 5,000 against the manager; repeated non-filing over several years triggers administrative strike-off (radiation) from the RCS and loss of good standing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO register confirmation and updated declaration of beneficial owners (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: UBO Register of the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any change in the register of partners or in beneficial ownership; as part of annual maintenance, at least one confirmation per calendar year, usually aligned with the annual partners' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines of up to EUR 1,250 per infraction under the Luxembourg UBO law and criminal penalties for false or incomplete declarations; refusal of certified good-standing statements; persistent non-compliance may be referred to the Public Prosecutor and can trigger administrative sanctions or judicial strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Chamber of Commerce contribution (cotisation annuelle à la Chambre de Commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable within 30 days of the annual invoice, ordinarily issued in the second calendar quarter on the basis of the prior-year Luxembourg taxable turnover; minimum contribution band applies to low-turnover SCSp structures
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory late-payment surcharge and enforced recovery through the Luxembourg tax collector (receveur); the contribution constitutes a privileged claim and prolonged non-payment may block issuance of Chamber certificates and impede RCS good-standing confirmations

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit by a Luxembourg réviseur d'entreprises agréé if the SCSp exceeds two of the three small-enterprise thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total exceeding EUR 4.4 million, net turnover exceeding EUR 8.8 million, or average workforce exceeding 50 employees; below these thresholds the statutory audit is waived, though partners may contractually require one
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as codified in the Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS and annual accounts, denominated in EUR; annual accounts must be prepared and deposited even for a tax-transparent SCSp where the commercial activity is carried on; IFRS is not mandatory for this standalone non-listed entity and applies only in defined consolidated or listed scenarios

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every transfer or issuance of partnership interests must be recorded in the SCSp's internal partnership register and, if it affects beneficial ownership, mirrored in the RCS UBO register within 30 days; annually, the managing partner must verify and re-confirm the full chain of natural persons holding directly or indirectly more than 25% of interests, voting rights or control; an outdated UBO filing leaves distributions to a new partner unprotected and exposes the entity to RCS fines

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $1,500 – $4,500 per annum (registered office, domiciliation and corporate agent services through a Luxembourg PFS)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $8,000 – $20,000 per annum for a small manufacturing partnership, where an audit is triggered; not required below the small-enterprise thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City aggregate rate: 17% CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge + municipal business tax). The SCSp is fiscally transparent; the rate applies to corporate partners/general partner on their taxable share of profits.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption (100% exempt dividends and capital gains on qualifying holdings), 80% exemption on qualifying IP income under the IP box, notional interest deduction on new equity, and ATAD-compliant minimisation. No statutory tax holiday for SCSp.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (indefinite carryforward; annual offset limited to EUR 1,000,000 plus 70% of taxable income exceeding EUR 1,000,000). Losses pass through to partners under SCSp transparency.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 600 (Déclaration de la société de personnes / Fiscally Transparent Partnership Annual Return) filed electronically via the Luxembourg Administration des contributions directes (ACD) secure portal eCDF / MyGuichet.lu.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than 31 December of the calendar year immediately following the fiscal year-end (i.e., within 12 months after closing); extensions may be granted by the tax office upon reasoned written request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the SCSp corporate name, registered office, RCS registration number (LU), legal form, and contact details of the Luxembourg tax representative if applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must ensure the SCSp remains duly registered; if no Luxembourg office exists, provide the tax representative's name and address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Indicate the general partner responsible for management, including its legal form, registered address, and tax residence, and attach an excerpt of the partnership agreement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the general partner is non-resident, confirm whether it performs management from Luxembourg and whether a Luxembourg permanent establishment is thereby created.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirm the SCSp's fiscally transparent classification and that no corporate income tax is assessed at the level of the partnership; enter the ACD transparency confirmation reference if obtained.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners should rely on the transparency classification and avoid reporting SCSp distributions as dividends for Luxembourg withholding tax purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the accounting profit, taxable income, and losses allocated among each partner in accordance with the partnership agreement's profit-sharing ratio.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate Luxembourg-source income to each non-resident partner; no withholding tax is normally due on profit distributions because the SCSp is transparent, but each partner remains taxable in its home jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose intercompany purchases, sales, royalties, management fees, and financing transactions with associated enterprises, including the arm's-length basis applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners should ensure the Luxembourg entity maintains contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation and a local file if the applicable thresholds are exceeded.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form 600 triggers a late-filing surcharge of up to 10% of the tax assessed, default interest of 0.8% per month on unpaid tax, and, after written demand, a coercive daily fine (astreinte) that can reach EUR 250 per day. Intentional non-filing or materially false declarations may result in criminal fines up to EUR 25,000 and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on actual profit distributions by an SCSp because of fiscal transparency; where a Luxembourg company pays a dividend to a non-resident corporate partner outside the participation exemption, the domestic rate is 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: For any Luxembourg withholding tax that does apply, the beneficial owner must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home state and submit it to the Luxembourg withholding agent or ACD together with Form 105 (withholding tax reclaim/relief request). The claim may be processed at source or by refund; substance documents and beneficial-ownership declarations are required to prevent treaty abuse.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic law imposes 0% withholding tax on outbound royalties and 0% withholding tax on ordinary bank or corporate-bond interest paid to non-residents. Under Luxembourg tax treaties, royalties are generally exempt or subject to very low WHT (0%), while interest rates range from 0% to 15% depending on the DTA; the EU Interest and Royalties Directive eliminates source tax in qualifying parent-subsidiary cases.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50,000,000 local net turnover triggers a full Luxembourg Local File; group consolidated revenue of EUR 750,000,000 triggers Master File and CbC Report. Below these thresholds, a contemporaneous Luxembourg TP file is nevertheless strongly recommended.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not maintain a standalone Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) regime, but applies the OECD principal purpose test, EU ATAD anti-abuse provisions, and the domestic abuse-of-law doctrine. An SCSp must demonstrate real economic activity in Luxembourg (office, staff, decision-making, risk control) and commercial substance to preserve tax transparency and treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of Luxembourg-source profits from the partnership return, false allocation schedules, or concealment of partner identities to avoid Luxembourg taxation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalties under Article 396 of the General Tax Law (AO): imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years and fines up to EUR 25,000, plus reassessment of unpaid taxes with interest and a late-filing surcharge of up to 10%.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managing partners and directors who knowingly execute the fraud are jointly and severally liable for the tax debt, subject to civil restitution orders, exit bans from Luxembourg during criminal proceedings, and imprisonment of up to 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an SCSp without commercial substance, using only a registered address and nominee management, to create tax treaty or pass-through benefits disproportionate to real economic activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ACD may disregard the legal form, refuse treaty benefits, recharacterize the income, deny the participation exemption, impose dividend/interest withholding taxes on deemed distributions, and impose administrative fines up to EUR 250,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally responsible for the tax re-established after disregard of the entity, may face disqualification as managers, asset seizures, travel bans, and criminal liability if the arrangement is deemed fraudulent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify and file the true beneficial owner(s) of the SCSp in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) within 30 days, or concealment of UBOs through nominee shareholders, bearer instruments, or shell entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 250,000 under the Luxembourg AML framework and RBE law; criminal sanctions for money laundering include imprisonment of up to 5 years; RBE registration can be suspended and bank account freezing/blocking orders may be issued.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for AML compliance failures; criminal fines and imprisonment apply if wilful money-laundering is proven; personal asset forfeiture, travel bans, and bans from serving as company directors are common ancillary sanctions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Implementing non-arm's-length intercompany arrangements involving the laser assembly entity (e.g., IP royalties, management fees, inventory allocation, or financing) with related parties in low-tax jurisdictions, while failing to prepare or maintain transfer pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The ACD may adjust taxable profits to an arm's-length level, apply default interest, impose documentation penalties up to EUR 5,000, and, if concealment is established, initiate criminal tax proceedings with fines up to EUR 25,000 and imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who are signatories to the intercompany agreements and responsible for TP documentation may be jointly liable for the primary tax adjustment plus interest; travel bans, management disqualification, and imprisonment are possible in cases of deliberate tax evasion.
